evals.prompt: I need to design a dimensional model for our e-commerce order data. We have orders, order line items, customers, and products coming from our Postgres source system. We need to support revenue reporting by product category, customer segment, and time period. Can you help me structure this?
evals.expected_output: The agent should check data-stack-context.md, clarify the business process and grain, recommend a star schema with fct_orders (grain = order line item), dim_customers, dim_products, and dim_dates, generate dbt model SQL stubs with surrogate keys, produce schema.yml with tests and documentation, and include warehouse-specific optimizations.
assertions: Checks for .claude/data-stack-context.md before asking warehouse questions
Clarifies the grain of the fact table (one row per order line item)
Recommends star schema as the default pattern
Generates a fact table (fct_orders) with surrogate keys using dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key
Generates dimension tables (dim_customers, dim_products, dim_dates) with surrogate keys
Includes foreign key relationships between fact and dimension tables
Produces schema.yml with column descriptions and tests (unique, not_null, relationships)
Includes warehouse-specific config (partitioning, clustering, dist/sort keys)
Classifies measures as additive, semi-additive, or non-additive
Runs dbt compile as validation step

evals.prompt: We're building a SaaS analytics platform and need to model subscription data. Subscriptions can be created, upgraded, downgraded, paused, resumed, and cancelled. We need to track MRR changes over time and understand churn by customer segment. We're on Snowflake.
evals.expected_output: The agent should design an accumulating snapshot fact table for subscription lifecycle, a periodic snapshot for MRR tracking, dimension tables for customers and plans, and handle SCD Type 2 for plan changes.
assertions: Checks for .claude/data-stack-context.md before proceeding
Identifies this as an accumulating snapshot fact pattern for subscription lifecycle
Recommends a periodic snapshot fact for daily/monthly MRR tracking
Designs dimension tables for customers and subscription plans
Addresses SCD Type 2 for tracking plan changes over time
Includes Snowflake-specific optimizations (clustering on date and customer_key)
Generates surrogate keys for all dimension tables
Produces schema.yml with tests including accepted_range for MRR values
Warns about grain explosion when joining subscriptions to customers

evals.prompt: Our marketing team wants a wide table for their campaigns data. They say star schema is too complex for them. Should I just build one big table with everything? We have campaign data, ad spend, impressions, clicks, and conversions across Google Ads and Facebook Ads.
evals.expected_output: The agent should evaluate the wide table vs star schema tradeoff, recommend the appropriate pattern based on the use case, and if a wide table is appropriate for the BI layer, still suggest proper staging and intermediate layers underneath.
assertions: Checks for .claude/data-stack-context.md
Evaluates wide table vs star schema tradeoffs honestly
Does not blindly reject the wide table approach — considers the audience (marketing team, BI tool)
Recommends proper staging layers even if a wide mart is the final output
Addresses grain carefully — ensures campaign-date or campaign-platform-date grain is explicit
Warns about the 'kitchen sink' anti-pattern if combining too many domains
Includes cost considerations for materializing a wide table
Generates dbt model SQL with proper ref() chains from staging to mart

evals.prompt: I need to design a data model for our healthcare patient encounters system on BigQuery. We have patient demographics, provider information, diagnoses (ICD-10 codes), procedures, and billing. Patients can have multiple encounters, each with multiple diagnoses and procedures.
evals.expected_output: The agent should design a model handling the complex many-to-many relationships in healthcare data, with BigQuery-specific optimizations, proper grain definition for each fact table, and careful handling of nested/repeated fields.
assertions: Checks for .claude/data-stack-context.md
Identifies the many-to-many relationships (encounters to diagnoses, encounters to procedures)
Defines clear grain for each fact table (e.g., one row per encounter-diagnosis pair for a bridge table)
Uses BigQuery-specific config: partition_by on encounter date, cluster_by on patient_key
Considers BigQuery nested/repeated fields (STRUCT/ARRAY) as an alternative to bridge tables
Generates surrogate keys using dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key
Produces schema.yml with column-level documentation
Includes a fanout check query to validate join cardinality
Does not use SELECT DISTINCT to mask join issues

evals.prompt: ugh our data is a mess. we have like 5 different tables that all have customer info and nobody knows which one is the source of truth. can you help me figure out how to structure this properly?
evals.expected_output: The agent should help consolidate customer data into a proper dimensional model with a single dim_customers as the source of truth, addressing SCD handling and deduplication.
assertions: Checks for .claude/data-stack-context.md
Asks clarifying questions about the 5 customer tables and their sources
Recommends a single dim_customers as the authoritative dimension
Addresses surrogate key strategy for merging multiple sources
Discusses SCD Type 1 vs Type 2 for tracking customer attribute changes
Warns about natural key drift across source systems
Suggests staging models for each source before consolidating
Generates schema.yml with uniqueness and not_null tests on the surrogate key

evals.prompt: I need to set up slowly changing dimensions for our product catalog. Products change prices and categories frequently and we need to track the historical values for accurate revenue reporting.
evals.expected_output: The agent should recognize this as primarily a slowly-changing-dimensions skill concern and defer to that skill, while briefly acknowledging the dimensional modeling context.
assertions: Checks for .claude/data-stack-context.md
Recognizes that SCD implementation is the primary concern, not general data modeling
Defers to or references the slowly-changing-dimensions skill for detailed SCD implementation
Does NOT generate full SCD snapshot configuration — that belongs to the SCD skill
May briefly explain how SCD Type 2 fits into the dimensional model architecture
Does not overstep into snapshot configuration or dbt snapshot strategy details
Acknowledges the relationship between dim tables and SCD but keeps scope to modeling decisions
